_comment: Every stop worth considering. 'routes' lists which route options it sits on — a stop shows up only when one of its routes is selected. 'detour' is MINUTES ONE WAY off the highway; the app doubles it and adds 'dwell' to show what it really costs the day. 'first' flags something Ada has no California equivalent for. 'big' means it's worth rebuilding the day around. 'winter' is the late-Dec / early-Jan caveat and is the field most likely to be wrong — verify before committing to any of them.

stops.name: Tehachapi Loop
stops.why: A freight train long enough to cross over the top of its own tail. It has been doing this since 1876 and it is still the thing railroad people drive across the country to watch.

stops.name: Calico Ghost Town
stops.why: A silver town that died in 1907 and got rebuilt as itself. Good legs-stretch two hours into the drive.
stops.winter: Cold and windy in December. Open year round.

stops.name: Route 66 Mother Road Museum
stops.why: Where the Route 66 thread starts. You'll be crossing and re-crossing the old road for the next 1,500 miles.
stops.winter: Closed Mon–Tue.

stops.name: Oatman
stops.why: Wild burros walk down the middle of the street and expect to be fed. The old Route 66 alignment to get there is a genuinely twisty mountain road.
stops.winter: The road over Sitgreaves Pass is narrow with no guardrail. Skip it in bad weather.

stops.name: Seligman
stops.why: The town that talked Arizona into preserving Route 66, and the one Pixar's Radiator Springs was drawn from. Two blocks long, entirely made of it.

stops.name: Grand Canyon, South Rim
stops.why: There is nothing to say about this one. An hour north of Williams, and the single best reason the northern route exists.
stops.winter: SOUTH rim is open all year — the North Rim is closed Dec through May. Snow on the rim in late December is normal and makes it better. Roads are plowed.

stops.name: Bearizona
stops.why: Drive-through wildlife park — wolves and bison walk past the car. Right at the Grand Canyon turn-off.
stops.winter: Open year round; the drive-through loop stays open in snow.

stops.name: Lowell Observatory
stops.why: Pluto was found here, from this hill, in 1930. Evening telescope viewing at 7,000 feet in winter air is about as good as the sky gets.
stops.winter: Open, and December nights are the clearest of the year — dress for 20°F standing still.

stops.name: Sunset Crater & Wupatki
stops.why: A black volcanic cinder field that erupted around 1085, and eight hundred year old pueblos on the far side of the same loop road.
stops.winter: The 34-mile loop road can close after snow. Check before turning off.

stops.name: Meteor Crater
stops.why: A mile-wide hole punched in the desert 50,000 years ago, six minutes off the interstate. The cheapest astonishment-per-minute on the entire route.
stops.winter: Open year round. Exposed and brutally windy on the rim in winter.

stops.name: Standin' on the Corner Park
stops.why: Yes, that corner. Four minutes off the freeway, takes fifteen, and you will have the song in your head until Albuquerque.

stops.name: Petrified Forest & Painted Desert
stops.why: The best-value stop of the whole trip: the 28-mile park road runs parallel to I-40 and drops you back on it, so most of the time isn't a detour at all. Fossil logs turned to solid quartz, and a badlands painted in bands of red and violet.
stops.winter: Open year round, gates close around 5pm in winter — go in the morning, not at dusk.

stops.name: Wigwam Motel
stops.why: Fifteen concrete teepees you can actually sleep in, built in 1950. Even if you don't stay, it's worth the photo.

stops.name: El Morro National Monument
stops.why: A sandstone bluff with a waterhole at its base, carved with signatures — Ancestral Puebloan petroglyphs, then Spanish conquistadors from 1605, then American cavalry. Four hundred years of people writing their name on the same rock.
stops.winter: Trails can be icy; the inscription loop is usually walkable.

stops.name: Sandia Peak Tramway
stops.why: Two and a half miles of cable up the face of the mountain to 10,378 feet. On a clear day you can see 11,000 square miles of New Mexico, and Albuquerque is a grid of lights underneath you at sunset.
stops.winter: Runs in winter. It's usually 25–30°F colder at the top than the parking lot — bring real coats.

stops.name: Old Town Albuquerque
stops.why: Adobe plaza from 1706, green chile on everything. Good dinner stop that isn't another interstate exit.
stops.winter: Farolitos — paper-bag lanterns — line the whole plaza through Christmas. It is genuinely beautiful and it's happening exactly when you'd pass through.

stops.name: Blue Swallow Motel & Tucumcari neon
stops.why: The best surviving stretch of Route 66 neon anywhere. Only works after dark — which makes it a good reason to stop for the night here rather than push on.

stops.name: Cadillac Ranch
stops.why: Ten Cadillacs buried nose-down in a field, and you are not just allowed to spray paint them, you're expected to. Buy a can in Amarillo first. This is the trip photo.
stops.winter: Open always, it's a field. Muddy after rain — wear the shoes you don't care about.

stops.name: Palo Duro Canyon
stops.why: The second largest canyon in the country, 800 feet deep, and almost nobody outside Texas knows it's there. Completely invisible until you're at the edge of it.
stops.winter: Open year round and quiet in winter. The road to the floor is steep.

stops.name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
stops.why: The 72-ounce steak that's free if you finish it in an hour. You are not going to do that, but you should eat here anyway.

stops.name: POPS 66 Soda Ranch
stops.why: A 66-foot lit soda bottle on old Route 66, and about 700 kinds of soda inside. Good lunch break outside Oklahoma City.

stops.name: Oklahoma City National Memorial
stops.why: 168 empty chairs, one for each person, arranged in the footprint of the building. The outdoor memorial is free and open all the time and takes twenty minutes.
stops.winter: Outdoor memorial open 24 hours.

stops.name: Little Rock Central High School
stops.why: Still a working high school, and the place nine teenagers walked into in 1957 behind the 101st Airborne. The visitor center across the street is a National Park site.
stops.winter: Visitor center closed Christmas Day.

stops.name: Hot Springs National Park
stops.why: A row of grand 1900s bathhouses built over natural hot springs, in the middle of a small town. You can still get in the water at two of them.
stops.winter: A hot bath in December is the entire point.

stops.name: Graceland
stops.why: Elvis's house, preserved exactly as 1977 left it. Expensive and completely worth it — the jungle room alone.
stops.winter: Closed Christmas Day. Decorated for Christmas from late November, which is how he actually had it.

stops.name: Sun Studio
stops.why: One small room where Elvis, Johnny Cash, Roy Orbison and Jerry Lee Lewis all recorded. Still a working studio at night. You can hold the microphone.

stops.name: National Civil Rights Museum
stops.why: Built around the Lorraine Motel, with Dr. King's room left as it was. One of the best museums in the country, and not a quick stop — give it a real afternoon.
stops.winter: Closed Tuesdays.

stops.name: Beale Street
stops.why: Live blues coming out of every door, and barbecue. If you only do one night out on the way east, do it here.

stops.name: Crossing the Mississippi
stops.why: The bridge itself. Half the continent drains through the water underneath you, and there is no river in California remotely like it. Just know it's coming so you look.

stops.name: Broadway
stops.why: Three blocks of honky-tonks, live band in every one, no cover in most. Loud and touristy and completely worth doing once.

stops.name: Ryman Auditorium
stops.why: The mother church of country music — a former revival hall with pews for seats and famously perfect sound. Self-guided tour by day.

stops.name: Great Smoky Mountains — Newfound Gap
stops.why: The most visited national park in the country, and the road climbs to 5,046 feet at the state line. Eastern mountains look nothing like the Sierra — older, softer, and wrapped in haze.
stops.winter: Newfound Gap Road closes with snow and ice, sometimes for days. Check nps.gov before committing. Clingmans Dome Road is closed all winter.

stops.name: Dollywood
stops.why: A full day, so only if the schedule has one. Its Christmas run is a genuine spectacle — several million lights.
stops.winter: Smoky Mountain Christmas runs through early January. Closed some weekdays in winter — check the calendar.

stops.name: Biltmore Estate
stops.why: The largest house in America, 250 rooms, finished in 1895. At Christmas they put a 35-foot tree in the banquet hall and light the whole place by candle in the evenings.
stops.winter: Christmas at Biltmore runs through early January and sells out — book weeks ahead. This one genuinely needs a reservation.

stops.name: Mount Mitchell
stops.why: 6,684 feet — the highest point anywhere east of the Mississippi. You can drive nearly to the top.
stops.winter: Reached via the Blue Ridge Parkway, which CLOSES for ice and snow all winter. Assume it's shut and treat an open day as a gift.

stops.name: NASCAR Hall of Fame
stops.why: You're driving straight past it and it's better than it sounds — the banked track display alone shows you how steep 33 degrees actually is.

stops.name: Georgia Aquarium
stops.why: One of the largest in the world, with whale sharks — which exist in about four aquariums on earth.
stops.winter: Book a timed ticket; the holiday week is its busiest of the year.

stops.name: MLK National Historical Park
stops.why: His birth home, Ebenezer Baptist where he preached, and his tomb — all on two blocks, all free.
stops.winter: Birth home tours are first-come and limited; get there early.

stops.name: Legacy Museum & National Memorial for Peace and Justice
stops.why: Eight hundred hanging steel columns, one for every county where a lynching happened. The most powerful museum in the American South and it costs five dollars.
stops.winter: Closed Tuesdays. Give it three hours or don't start.

stops.name: USS Alabama Battleship
stops.why: A World War II battleship you walk through top to bottom, plus a submarine, four minutes off I-10.

stops.name: First look at the Gulf
stops.why: Warm, flat, pale green water and sand like sugar. Nothing about it resembles the Pacific she grew up on — and in December you'll have the beach to yourselves.
stops.winter: Too cold to swim, perfect to walk.

stops.name: The French Quarter
stops.why: Beignets at Café du Monde, brass bands on Royal Street, two hundred year old ironwork. There is nowhere else in the country that feels like this and it is worth an overnight, not a drive-through.
stops.winter: You'd be here right around New Year's — which is spectacular and also means book a room early and expect crowds.

stops.name: Oak Alley Plantation
stops.why: A quarter-mile corridor of 300-year-old live oaks, and an unflinching museum about the people who were enslaved there. Both halves matter.

stops.name: Space Center Houston
stops.why: The actual Apollo mission control room, restored to 1969 down to the ashtrays, and a complete Saturn V lying on its side in a building built around it.
stops.winter: Open through the holidays except Christmas Day. Very busy that week.

stops.name: The Alamo
stops.why: Smaller than everyone expects and right in the middle of downtown. Free, and it takes an hour.

stops.name: San Antonio River Walk
stops.why: A river one level below the street, lined with restaurants for miles. In December and early January the whole thing is strung with lights over the water and you take a boat through it.
stops.winter: The holiday lights run through early January — you would be passing at exactly the right moment. Verify the end date before counting on it.

stops.name: Natural Bridge Caverns
stops.why: The largest commercial cave in Texas, and 70°F underground no matter what the weather does.
stops.winter: Weather-proof. A good rainy-day answer.

stops.name: Balmorhea State Park
stops.why: A 1.3-acre spring-fed pool in the middle of nowhere, 72°F all year, with fish in it. Utterly surreal after four hours of West Texas.
stops.winter: Open in winter but check — it has closed for long repair stretches. Confirm before detouring.

stops.name: Marfa Lights Viewing Area
stops.why: Unexplained lights on the horizon that people have been arguing about since 1883. There's an official pull-out with a viewing platform. Might see nothing. That's part of it.
stops.winter: Needs full dark and a clear night. Only worth it if you're sleeping nearby anyway.

stops.name: Carlsbad Caverns
stops.why: You walk down into it through a hole in the desert and end up 750 feet underground in a room the size of six football fields. A big detour and one of the great places on the continent.
stops.winter: Fully weather-proof — 56°F underground always. The bat flights are summer only, so winter costs you nothing but the drive. Entry reservations required.

stops.name: White Sands National Park
stops.why: 275 square miles of pure white gypsum dunes. You buy a plastic saucer at the gift shop and sled down them. There is nothing like it anywhere else on earth and the detour off I-10 is worth every mile.
stops.winter: Open in winter and the light is best then. It closes for a few hours at a time for missile range tests — check the park's closure page the morning of.

stops.name: Scenic Drive Overlook
stops.why: One overlook, two countries, three states. El Paso and Ciudad Juárez spread out below as one continuous city split by a line.
stops.winter: Best at dusk when both sides light up.

stops.name: Tombstone
stops.why: The OK Corral, Boot Hill, and a main street that leans hard into it. Touristy in a way that's honestly fine.
stops.winter: Mild and pleasant in winter.

stops.name: Saguaro National Park
stops.why: Forests of cactus fifty feet tall and two hundred years old. The loop drive at sunset is the one.
stops.winter: Peak season — winter is the best time of year to be here.

stops.name: Pima Air & Space Museum
stops.why: Four hundred aircraft parked in the desert, including an SR-71 and a Boeing 787. Add the bus tour of the boneyard next door — 4,000 mothballed military planes in rows.
stops.winter: Boneyard tours are weekdays only and need advance booking.

stops.name: Desert Botanical Garden
stops.why: The best desert-plant collection anywhere, and in December they light the paths with thousands of luminarias after dark.
stops.winter: Las Noches de las Luminarias runs through early January and needs a timed ticket.

stops.name: Joshua Tree National Park
stops.why: The Cottonwood entrance is right on I-10, so this is a cheap detour on the last full day. Boulder piles and the trees themselves, which look invented.
stops.winter: Winter is the good season. Nights drop below freezing.

stops.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
stops.why: Rotating cable car from the desert floor to 8,500 feet in ten minutes — from palm trees to pine snow. If you skipped Sandia, take this one.
stops.winter: There is usually snow at the top while it's 70°F at the bottom, which is the whole trick.

stops.name: Griffith Observatory
stops.why: Free, and the view of the whole basin at night is the last big thing before the drive turns into just getting home.
stops.winter: Closed Mondays. Parking is genuinely awful — go early or late.

stops.name: Salvation Mountain
stops.why: A hillside one man covered in half a million gallons of paint over thirty years. Strange, sincere, and completely unlike anything else.
stops.winter: Winter is the only tolerable time — it's 115°F here in summer.

stops.name: The Sixth Floor Museum
stops.why: The Texas School Book Depository, from the window itself. They preserved the corner exactly as it was found and the whole story is told from inside the room.
stops.winter: Open through the holidays except Christmas Day. Timed tickets.

stops.name: Fort Worth Stockyards
stops.why: A longhorn cattle drive down a brick street twice a day, every day, plus the honky-tonks around it. Cornier than Nashville and somehow better for it.

stops.name: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
stops.why: Across the street from the 16th Street Baptist Church and Kelly Ingram Park, where the fire hoses were turned on children in 1963. The museum and those two blocks are one thing.
stops.winter: Closed Mondays.

stops.name: Vicksburg National Military Park
stops.why: A 16-mile drive through the siege lines above the Mississippi, plus a Union ironclad raised out of the river mud a century later.
stops.winter: Open year round, quiet in winter.

stops.name: Hoover Dam
stops.why: 726 feet of concrete wedged into Black Canyon in the middle of the Depression. You can walk out on the bypass bridge and look straight down the face of it for free.
stops.winter: Open year round and December is the pleasant time to be here. Security screening on the dam road.

stops.name: The Strip
stops.why: Whatever you think of it, there is nothing else like it, and walking it at night once is worth doing. The Bellagio fountains are free and run every half hour.
stops.winter: Cold at night in December — colder than people expect in a desert.

stops.name: Seven Magic Mountains
stops.why: Seven stacks of boulders painted in fluorescent colors standing alone in the desert south of Vegas. Ten minutes, free, and it photographs better than almost anything on the trip.

stops.name: Kelso Dunes, Mojave National Preserve
stops.why: Six hundred foot sand dunes that boom audibly when you slide down them. Almost nobody stops, which is most of the appeal.
stops.winter: Winter is the only comfortable season. Last few miles are graded dirt.
